title: S6 - Web foundation and design system
description: Weeks 11-12. Exit: the web app builds and deploys through CI, staff can sign in and reach the right workspace, and the approved designs, design system and motion system are ready for feature work.
goal: Give the web app a professional visual identity, motion system and secure foundation before any feature screen is built.
entry_criteria: Confirm owners and realistic capacity before starting.
Required predecessor deliverables are available or scheduled in dependency order.

exit_criteria.description: All sprint issues meet their acceptance criteria and completion evidence requirements.
Sign in as a therapist and as an administrator, land in the right workspace, and walk through the component gallery showing interactive cards, motion and every component state.

demo: Sign in as a therapist and as an administrator, land in the right workspace, and walk through the component gallery showing interactive cards, motion and every component state.
risks: Feature screens started before the designs are approved will need rework; keep the design review as a real gate.
Too much motion slows clinical work; every animation must have a purpose and respect reduced-motion settings.

execution_plan.first_week: Work prerequisites first; review integration and design risks midweek.
execution_plan.second_week: Integrate, execute acceptance checks, fix defects and demonstrate the sprint outcome.
execution_plan.capacity_policy: Estimates are provisional; reserve approximately 20% of actual team capacity for integration and defects.

acceptance_criteria.description: TypeScript runs in strict mode, and typecheck, lint, test and build all pass from a clean clone.
docs/PLAN.md records the pinned stack and the reason for each runtime dependency.
Environment values live in ignored web/.env with web/.env.example as the template; only the Supabase URL and publishable key are used.

A build check fails if a service-role key or any other secret appears in the built files.
docs/operations/DEVELOPMENT.md explains how to run the web app against local Supabase.

acceptance_criteria.description: docs/architecture/WEB-DESIGN.md records the direction: layout grid, type scale, data density, use of the motion arc, and what the design deliberately avoids, such as default dashboard templates.

High-fidelity designs cover sign-in, therapist home, patient list, patient record, assignment editor, progress, and the administrator overview, accounts, links, catalogue and activity pages, at 1440, 1024 and 768 px wide.
Each design shows its loading, empty, error and confirmation states, not only the filled state.
Interactions for cards, tables, dialogs and page changes are specified alongside the designs.
Colours meet WCAG 2.1 AA contrast, Amber stays reserved for caution and hold, and progress is always also stated in text, as in docs/architecture/UI-UX.md.
The project owner reviews and approves the designs before S7 feature screens start, and the approval is recorded.

acceptance_criteria.description: Tokens come from the motion arc system (Ink #0D2B36, Lagoon #0E7C86, Sprout #1B7F45, Mist #F1F6F5, Amber #E8A33D), and components use tokens rather than hard-coded values.
Bricolage Grotesque is self-hosted under its OFL licence for headings and key numbers; no font loads from a third party.
The library covers buttons, fields, selects, dialogs, confirmation dialogs, toasts, cards, tables, tabs, pagination, tooltips, avatars, status pills, skeletons and empty states.
Every interactive component has designed hover, focus, pressed, disabled, loading and error states, and works by keyboard alone.
A component gallery shows each component in every state.
Toasts match Android: 5 seconds, a close button and a time bar.

issues.title: Add interactive cards and the motion system
issues.description: Make the interface feel responsive and alive without slowing clinical work: cards that react to the pointer, transitions that explain where you went, and numbers and arcs that move with meaning.
issues.requirements: User request, 2026-11-05: web app for therapists and administrators, in TypeScript

acceptance_criteria.description: Motion tokens define durations, easing and springs in one place; no screen sets its own timing.
Cards lift on hover with a highlight that follows the pointer, settle under a press, and show the same emphasis on keyboard focus.
Cards can expand in place to reveal detail, and opening a record from a row or card carries through to the record header as a shared transition.
Page changes move by navigation depth, as on Android. Lists stagger in on first load only, not on every refresh, and skeletons crossfade to content.
MotionArc and the draggable RangeArc are ported with an animated sweep, and key numbers roll to their new value.
The prefers-reduced-motion setting replaces movement with simple fades, and this is tested.
Animations use transform and opacity only, hold 60 frames per second on a 50-row page, and never delay input. Motion is never the only sign of a state change.

issues.description: Use the same single sign-in rules as Android, and protect patient data on shared clinic computers.

functions.description: Warn and then sign out after inactivity, and clear all patient data.
functions.kind: planned capability; implementation names may change

acceptance_criteria.description: One sign-in page with no role choice, using the same order as Android: administrator, then therapist, then patient.
An account with several staff roles can switch workspace, and that choice ends at sign-out.
A patient-only account is told to use the mobile app and no patient data loads. The web app has no sign-up.
Password recovery uses the same emailed code as Android, and disabled accounts cannot enter.
After 15 minutes of inactivity, with a 1-minute warning, the session ends. Signing out in one tab ends every tab.
Signing out clears all cached data. Nothing containing patient data is written to browser storage; only the auth session is stored.
A workspace the account does not hold cannot be reached by URL, proven by a browser test.

acceptance_criteria.description: Database types are generated from the migrations, and CI fails when they are out of date.
All reads and writes go through one typed layer. Failures show a friendly message with Retry, and raw server errors never reach the screen.
A contract test runs the web queries against local Supabase, including the history embedding and the catalogue exercises(id,owner_id) query.
The shell has a role-aware sidebar, a top bar with account and language controls, and breadcrumbs, and works from 768 to 1920 px wide with no horizontal page scroll.
All text exists in English and Filipino, CI fails when keys or placeholders differ, and the language choice is remembered.
